info.name: Save n Spend API
info.description:
Local API for the Save n Spend app (Express + Mongo, port 7019).

## Setup
1. Start the API: `cd apps/api && npm run dev`
2. (Optional) seed test data: `npm run seed` — creates **sagnik@email.com / sagnik123** and **bipasha@email.com / bipasha123**
3. Run **Auth → Login (Sagnik)** once — its test script stores `accessToken` as a collection variable and every other request inherits it via Bearer auth.

## Conventions
- Every response uses the envelope `{ success, statusCode, message, data }`.
- **Money is integer paise** (₹1 = 100 paise). `amount` is always positive; `type` gives the sign.
- All `/:id` routes are ownership-scoped: another user's id returns 404, leaking nothing.
- Create/POST helper scripts store `accountId` / `categoryId` / `transactionId` collection variables so the `/:id` requests chain without copy-pasting ids.
- The same applies to the later folders: creating a person, investment, budget, bill, goal, trip or trip expense stores `personId` / `investmentId` / `budgetId` / `billId` / `goalId` / `tripId` / `tripExpenseId`. `notificationId` is the one you set by hand, from an item in **Notifications → List**.
- Run **Accounts → Create person account** and **Create investment account** before the Trips and Investments folders; they need those ids.

item.name: Health
item.description: Liveness probe — outside /api/v1, no auth.

request.description: Returns `{ ok: true }` when the server is up. Does not touch the DB.

item.name: Auth
item.description: Register does NOT auto-login (separate flows by design). Login's test script auto-saves `accessToken`.

request.description:
Body: `name` (min 2 chars), `email`, `password` (min 8 chars).

Atomic register-seeding inside a Mongo transaction: creates the user → a starter **Cash** account → copies the default category set (per-user copies) → sets `prefs.defaultAccount` to the Cash account. All-or-nothing.

Does NOT return a token — log in afterwards.

response.name: 201 Created
409 Conflict (duplicate email)

exec: // Auto-populate the collection's accessToken from a successful login.
console.log('accessToken saved — all requests are now authenticated.');

request.description: Seed test user 1. On 200, the test script stores `data.accessToken` into the `accessToken` collection variable — every protected request inherits it via the collection-level Bearer auth. Token expiry: 7 days.

exec: // Switch the whole collection to Bipasha's session (handy for IDOR/404 checks).

request.description: Seed test user 2. Use to verify ownership scoping: log in here, then hit a `/:id` saved from Sagnik's session — it must 404.
Returns the logged-in user (from the Bearer token). The mobile app calls this on boot to validate a stored token.

response.name: 200 OK

request.description:
Body: `currentPassword` (any non-empty string) and `newPassword` (min 8 chars). Strict-by-schema, but the check is against the current password rather than the token alone, so a picked-up unlocked phone cannot rotate it.

Rate limited with the same 10-per-15-minutes limiter as login and register.

This changes the seeded user's password: change it back afterwards, or the **Login (Sagnik)** request will stop working.

item.name: Users
item.description: Profile & preferences.

request.description:
Strict body — unknown keys are rejected.
- `prefs.defaultAccount`: account id or null
- `prefs.budgetCycleDay`: 1–28
- `prefs.notifications.billReminderLead`: 1 | 3 | 7 (days)
- `pushToken`: optional string (Expo push token)

All fields optional — send only what changes.

response.name: 200 OK

request.description: The signed-in user's profile and prefs (`prefs.timeZone`, `prefs.notifications`, `prefs.defaultAccount`). `/auth/me` returns the same document and is what the app boots from.

Soft-deletes the account: stamps `deactivatedAt` (which locks it out of `/auth/me`, and so out of the app), drops it from the reminder job and clears `pushToken`. Data is kept. Responds `200` with `message: "Account deactivated"` and `data: null`.

**Destructive for the session** — the token stops working afterwards. Do not run against a user you still need.

item.name: Accounts
item.description: Per-user accounts. Balances are in integer paise. Delete = archive (`isArchived: true`), never a hard delete — transactions reference accounts.

request.description: Active (non-archived) accounts for the logged-in user.

response.name: 200 OK
response.body:
{
  "success": true,
  "statusCode": 200,
  "message": "Accounts fetched successfully",
  "data": [
    {
      "_id": "6a568002927536ee5cba3cbd",
      "userId": "6a568001927536ee5cba3c9d",
      "name": "Cash",
      "type": "cash",
      "balance": 1011000,
      "startingBalance": 1000000,
      "icon": "wallet",
      "color": "success",
      "isArchived": false
    },
    {
      "_id": "6a568002927536ee5cba3cbf",
      "userId": "6a568001927536ee5cba3c9d",
      "name": "HDFC Bank",
      "type": "bank",
      "balance": 12535200,
      "startingBalance": 5000000,
      "icon": "bank",
      "color": "info",
      "isArchived": false

request.description:
Strict body.
- `type`: bank | credit_card | cash | wallet
- `startingBalance`: integer paise (₹25,000 = 2500000). Becomes the initial `balance`.
- Credit cards use **signed negative balances** (negative = owed) — start one at 0 or negative.

Test script saves `data._id` → `{{accountId}}` for the `/:id` requests below.
Ownership-scoped: another user's id → 404.

Editable: `name`, `type`, `icon`, `color` — all optional, strict.

**No `balance` here by design** — balances only move via transactions (use an adjustment transaction to reconcile).
Soft delete: sets `isArchived: true`. Archived accounts drop out of List but historical transactions keep referencing them.
An account of `type: "person"` — someone who owes you or is owed. People are what a trip's `members` and a split's `owedBy` point at. Test script saves `data._id` → `{{personId}}`.

An account of `type: "investment"` — a holding. For investments `startingBalance` is what has been invested so far (the cost basis), `currentValue` is what it is worth today (omit it and it is worth exactly what went in), `investedSince` cannot be in the future, and `investedHow` is `sip` or `lump`. `investmentKind` is a free label up to 40 chars.

Test script saves `data._id` → `{{investmentId}}`, used by the Investments folder.

Strict body: `ids` — the user's **whole** list of active account ids, in the order the user left it, front to back (a whole-list write, so two rows can never claim one slot). Every id must be the caller's own, non-archived, and listed once, otherwise `400`.

Responds `{ reordered: <count> }`.

Declared above `PATCH /accounts/:id`, which would otherwise match `reorder` as an id.

Reconcile an account against what the bank says it holds. `balance` is the **target** balance in integer paise, not a delta, and is signed and unbounded (a credit card is negative as it is used). Optional `note` (1-120 chars).

The server writes the *difference* as an adjustment transaction, which keeps the balance invariant: it moves the balance but stays out of income and expense totals. Strict body.

item.description: Per-user copies (defaults seeded at register). 2-level tree via `parent` (null = top-level); the 2-level limit is enforced in the controller. Delete = archive.

request.description: The user's full active set — parents and children in one flat list (`parent` links them).

request.description:
Strict body.
- `kind`: expense | income (fixed at creation)
- `parent`: a **top-level** category id, or null/omitted. Passing a child id as parent → 400 (only 2 levels).

Test script saves `data._id` → `{{categoryId}}`.

response.name:
400 Bad Request (3rd level attempted)

2.8.6: the name "Trips" (any case) is the built-in category's and is refused: 400 `invalid_input` "Trips is a built-in category".

request.description: Editable: `name`, `icon`, `color`. `kind` and `parent` are immutable — recreate instead.
Soft delete (`isArchived: true`). Historical transactions keep the reference.

Strict body: `ids` — one **sibling set** (the top-level categories, or the children of one parent) in the order the user left it, front to back. A whole-set write, so two rows can never claim one slot.

item.name: Transactions
item.description:
The balance engine: every create/edit/delete atomically moves account balances inside a Mongo transaction.
- expense: −amount on `account`
- income: +amount on `account`
- transfer: −amount on `account`, +amount on `toAccount` (ONE document)
- positiveAdjustment / negativeAdjustment: ±amount on `account` (reconciliation; excluded from spending insights)

`amount` is always positive integer paise. `type` is immutable after creation.

query.description: Filtering by a parent automatically includes its children
exclude | only | entries (2.8.6: everyday rows plus one kind:"trip" row per closed trip on its close day; category=trips picks only those)
ISO date — must be paired with endDate
ISO date — must be paired with startDate

request.description:
A page (`Paginated<ITransaction>` in packages/types): `data` is `{ items, page, limit, hasNextPage, total }`, newest first. `total` counts every match across all pages. There is no `docs` or `totalDocs` (older APIs sent them).

Gotchas:
- Query values are NOT quoted: `?type=income`, never `?type="income"`.
- `startDate`/`endDate` must be sent together (single one → 400).
- `category` is a plain id in each row (no populate) — the client resolves names from its own store.

expense/income branch (discriminated union): requires `account`, `category`, `title`. Optional: `note`, `location`, `receiptUrl`, `paymentMode` (cash|upi|card|transfer), `occurredAt` (ISO — server stamps now when omitted).

₹450 = 45000 paise, debited from the account atomically.

Test script saves `data._id` → `{{transactionId}}`.

response.name: 201 Created
response.body:
{
  "success": true,
  "statusCode": 201,
  "message": "Transaction created!",
  "data": {
    "_id": "6a5fcad5abf73860c118ea63",
    "userId": "6a568001927536ee5cba3c9d",
    "type": "expense",
    "amount": 45000,
    "account": "6a568002927536ee5cba3cbd",
    "category": "6a568001927536ee5cba3c9f",
    "title": "Starbucks",
    "note": "Cold brew with friends",
    "location": "Connaught Place",
    "paymentMode": "upi",
    "occurredAt": "2026-07-21T14:30:00.000Z"
  }
}

request.description: Same branch as expense — `type: income` credits the account instead. Use an income-kind category id.

Transfer branch: `account` (source) + `toAccount` (destination), NO `category`/`title` (strict — they're rejected). ONE document; the engine debits source and credits destination atomically.

Same-account transfer → 400 "Cannot transfer to same account". Replace the placeholder ids with two real account ids.

response.name: 400 Bad Request (same account)

request.description:
Adjustment branch: `type` = positiveAdjustment | negativeAdjustment, `account` required, `title` optional, NO category/toAccount.

Reconciliation flow: client computes `delta = target − current`; positive delta → positiveAdjustment, negative → negativeAdjustment, `amount = |delta|`. Moves the balance but is auto-excluded from spending insights.
Ownership-scoped single fetch — powers the mobile Edit prefill. Foreign id → 404.

Strict body — editable: `amount`, `account`, `toAccount`, `category`, `title`, `note`, `location`, `receiptUrl`, `paymentMode`, `occurredAt`. **`type` is immutable** (delete + recreate to change kind).

The engine reverts the OLD effects, applies the NEW ones — balances stay exact. Verify: check the account balance before/after; it should shift by exactly the delta.
HARD delete (transactions are leaf records — nothing references them) with a balance revert: the account gets the money back before the doc is removed, atomically.

query.description: exclude | only | entries (2.8.6: sums the trips=entries list's rows)

request.description: Income, expense and net for a range, computed server-side so the Activity summary card adds up to the rows beneath it. `startDate` and `endDate` (ISO dates) must be given together, or both omitted for all time. `trips=exclude` keeps trip rows out (the everyday list); `trips=only` is the trips view; unset means everything.

Up to 150 recent titles (last 12 months, expenses and income, trip rows excluded) ranked by how often they recur. Each carries `type`, `category`, `count`, `lastAmount` and `lastTransactionId`, so a quick-log chip can prefill and repeat a habitual transaction without another round trip.

Reclassifies an existing **expense** as a contribution: it becomes a transfer into `toAccount` (an investment account) and loses its category. Strict body with `toAccount` only. Balances move accordingly.

Uses `{{transactionId}}` (saved by the Create expense request) and `{{investmentId}}`.

The same reclassification over a batch, in one database transaction — "move the past payments too" after setting up a SIP from a suggestion. `transactionIds`: 1-60 ids. `toAccount`: the investment account. Strict body.

item.name: Dashboard
item.description: The Home tab's data. All three are read-only and bucketed in the user's stored time zone.

query.description: ISO datetime of the device's last open
2.8.6: month | year | all. The four tile figures cover it; adds period, periodStart, firstRecordAt, previous, netWorthAtStart
2.8.6: the trips rule (each closed trip once, on its close day; open trips nowhere). Off: the 2.8.5 figures

request.description:
The month's income, expense and net, this week's figures, net worth and its trend, streak, biggest expense, and the "since you last opened" digest.

- `month`: `YYYY-MM`, defaults to the current month in the user's zone.
- `since`: ISO datetime of **this device's** last open, so the digest is relative to this phone's last visit rather than a server-side session.

2.8.4: `tripExpenses`, `weekTripExpense` and `flowTrend[].tripExpense` are the trip part of `expenses`, `weekExpense` and `expense` (which still include trips). Everyday spending is the difference. `netWorthTrend` counts the same accounts as `netWorth`, so an archived account moves no past point. `biggestEverydayExpense` is the biggest expense without trips; `sinceLastOpened.tripSpent` is the trip part of `spent`.

2.8.6: `period=month|year|all` (Home's switch) makes `income`, `expenses`, `tripExpenses` and `savings` cover that period and adds `period`, `periodStart`, `firstRecordAt`, `previous` (null for All time or when records start inside the period) and `netWorthAtStart`. `trips=entries` applies the trips rule. Without either, the 2.8.5 body.

query.description: 2.8.6: the trips rule (each closed trip once, on its close day; open trips nowhere). Off: the 2.8.5 figures

request.description:
The finance health score with its pillars, band and hints, as shown on the Health screen.

2.8.4: `value` and `hint` use exact paise and one-decimal percentages (`20.5%`, `₹1,500.00`). The buffer pillar and `runwayMonths` use everyday spending (trips left out); the savings hint adds "including trips" when the window had any.

query.description: 2.8.6: the trips rule (each closed trip once, on its close day; open trips nowhere). Off: the 2.8.5 figures

request.description:
The Home tab's insight cards for the current month: goal progress, no-spend days, pace against the average, and the weekday pattern. No query parameters.

2.8.4: `everyday` holds `noSpendDays`, `weekdayHeatmap` and `pace` again with trip spending left out (a trip-only day is a no-spend day). `forYou` and `pace` keep trips.

item.name: Budgets
item.description: Monthly limits per category. `month` is `YYYY-MM`. `limit` is integer paise.

request.description: Budgets for a month with spend against each, in the user's zone. `month` defaults to the current month.
Strict body: `category` (a category id), `month` (`YYYY-MM`), `limit` (positive integer paise). Test script saves `data._id` → `{{budgetId}}`.
Only the `limit` can change (strict, positive integer paise).
Removes the budget for that category and month.

item.name: Bills
item.description: Bills and SIPs. A bill with `toInvestment` set is a SIP — paying it moves money into that holding instead of spending it.

request.description: All bills, or only one status.

Strict body.
- `name`, `amount` (positive integer paise), `dueDate` required.
- `recurring` + `frequency` (`monthly` | `yearly`) for a repeating bill.
- `reminderDays`: whole days before the due date, 0 or more.
- `category` / `account`: ids; `category` may be null.
- `toInvestment`: an investment account id (or null) — makes this a SIP.

Test script saves `data._id` → `{{billId}}`.
A bill that funds a holding. Paying it records a transfer from `account` into `toInvestment` rather than an expense.
Any create field, all optional, strict.
Removes the bill.

Marks the bill paid and records the transaction (or the SIP transfer). Optional body `account` picks the account to charge; otherwise the bill's own account, then the user's `prefs.defaultAccount`. `400` if none of those resolves. A SIP bill moves the money into its holding as a transfer, not an expense.

`400` when the bill is already paid, or when a recurring bill is already handled for the current period. A recurring bill rolls its `dueDate` forward after payment.
Advances a **recurring** bill's due date by one period without paying it. `400` for a non-recurring bill, or when this period is already handled. No body.

item.name: Goals
item.description: Savings goals. `target` and `saved` are integer paise.

request.description: The user's goals, oldest first.
Strict body: `name` (1-60 chars), `target` (positive integer paise); optional `icon`, `color`, `deadline`. Test script saves `data._id` → `{{goalId}}`.
Any create field, all optional, strict. `deadline` can be set to `null` to clear it.
Removes the goal.
Adds `amount` (positive integer paise) to `saved`, then checks for a goal milestone notification. Strict body.

item.name: Insights
item.description: The Insights tab. Windows are whole periods in the user's zone; the future is not allowed.

query.description: 2.8.6: the trips rule. Trips becomes a ranked byCategory slice with share and children (closedOn); adds entryCount

request.description:
Trend, income vs expense series, category breakdown, accounts, heatmaps, movers and totals for one window.

- `period`: `day` | `week` | `month` | `year` (default `month`).
- `offset`: whole periods back from the current one; `0` = current, `-1` = previous. Never positive.

2.8.4: `incomeVsExpense[].tripExpense` is the trip part of `expense`. Every `byCategory` slice but Trips has `share`, its share of everyday spending to one decimal; with `uncategorised.share` they add up to 100.0. `trend[].tripAmount` and `previousTrend[].tripAmount` are the trip part of each bucket; `avgDailyEverydaySpendCurrent`/`Previous` are the daily averages without trips. `byAccount` still includes trips.

query.description: 2.8.6: shareOfSpend over all spending with each closed trip once; the category's own figures never hold trips

request.description:
One category over one window: its total, children, day-by-day trend and recent rows. Same `period` / `offset` as the summary. `404` for another user's category.

2.8.4: `shareOfEverydaySpend` divides by everyday spending (trips left out); `shareOfSpend` still divides by all spending.

item.name: Notifications
item.description: The in-app feed behind the bell. It is the source of truth for what was sent — push is best-effort.

request.description: Newest first. `data` is a page plus `unread`: `{ items, page, limit, hasNextPage, total, unread }`; `unread` counts the whole feed, not the page. `limit` max is 50 (default 20).
Idempotent: the first read's timestamp is kept and a repeat still answers `200`. Set `{{notificationId}}` from an item in the list above.
Marks every unread notification read. No body.

item.name: Highlights
item.description: Sentences the server computes from the account's own numbers — what the charts don't say out loud.

query.description: 2.8.6: the trips rule (each closed trip once, on its close day; open trips nowhere). Off: the 2.8.5 figures

request.description:
The current highlights, materiality-ranked and capped. See the Insights engine doc for the rules.

2.8.4: titles and bodies use exact paise, one-decimal percentages and the true minus. "Spending" means everyday spending: `catch_all_heavy` divides by it, and `savings_rate_move`'s body says "including trips" when the month had trip spending.
Past highlights, newest first. `data` is a page: `{ items, page, limit, hasNextPage, total }`. `limit` max is 100.

item.name: Recurring
item.description: Detected repeating payments that could become bills.

request.description: Suggestions found in the transaction history that look like a bill or SIP. Each has a `key`.
Strict body: `key` (1-200 chars), taken from a suggestion in the list. A dismissed suggestion is not offered again.

item.name: Reviews
item.description: Month and week reviews of a closed period.

query.description: -1 = the one that just closed; must be negative
2.8.6: the trips rule. Trips ranked in categories with share and children

request.description:
A computed review of a **closed** period.

- `period`: `week` | `month` (default `month`).
- `offset`: whole periods back, **negative**: `-1` (default) is the one that just closed. `0`, the period containing today, is rejected.

2.8.4: `tripExpenses` and `previousTripExpenses` are the trip part of `expenses` and `previousExpenses`. Each category but Trips has `share` (one decimal, of everyday spending, over every slice), and `uncategorised` is the everyday spend with no category. `netWorth` counts today's accounts only. The verdict and timeline use exact paise and one decimal; the timeline's biggest expense is the everyday one. The heaviest/lightest week moment counts everyday spending only.

item.name: Cash Flow
item.description: A forward look at the bank balance.

request.description: What is coming in and going out between now and the end of next month, and what that leaves in the bank each day: bills and SIPs on their due dates, income on the day it usually arrives, and typical everyday spending in between. No query parameters.

item.name: Investments
item.description: Holdings are accounts of `type: investment`. Create one under Accounts → Create investment account, which saves `{{investmentId}}`.

request.description: Totals, per-holding invested / current / gain and yearly return (`annualReturn`, `annualReturnStatus`), allocation by kind, and this month's contributions.
Month-end history of the portfolio and of every holding: `points` (value, invested, contributions), `growth` (monthly change from value updates) and per-holding series. Drives the Trends tab.

Everything the Investments statement needs in one response: holdings, totals, the trend and the full `ledger` of contributions, redemptions and value updates. Period and scope are applied on the client.
Transactions on one holding, including value updates (adjustments). `400` for an invalid id, `404` if it is not the caller's investment.

Corrects what was invested, since when and how, without touching today's value. Strict body, all optional:
- `invested`: the **total** invested, integer paise (min 0). The server works out the opening amount after the contributions and redemptions already recorded; `400` if it would be negative.
- `investedSince`: date, not in the future, or null.
- `investedHow`: `sip` | `lump` | null.

Removes the holding and everything on it, in one database transaction. Archiving (`DELETE /accounts/:id`) keeps history; this does not.

Required query `mode`:
- `undo` — every money move into and out of it is reversed and deleted; the money goes back where it came from.
- `keep` — each transfer becomes a balance correction on the other account, so that account's balance does not move.

SIP bills funding it are deleted too. **Destructive.**

item.name: Backup
item.description: Whole-account export and restore.

request.description: Everything the account holds as one JSON document (`version: 1`): preferences, accounts, categories, transactions, budgets, bills, goals, and trips with their expenses. Save the response as a file.

**Replaces the account's data** with a backup, in one database transaction. The body is a backup document (the Export response's `data`) plus `"confirm": true`, the server-side half of the hold-to-confirm guard. `trips` and `tripExpenses` are optional, so a backup from before trips still restores.

Rate limited to 5 per hour. Responds `{ counts, user }` — the fresh `user` so the client picks up the restored time zone.

The body below is an empty-account skeleton; paste a real export in its place.

item.name: Diagnostics
item.description: Support tooling behind Settings → Diagnostics.

body.raw:
{
  "message": "Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'name')",
  "stack": "TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined\n    at InvestmentDetail (app/investment-detail.tsx:120)",
  "screen": "/investment-detail",
  "requestId": "7K2QXB",
  "appVersion": "2.5.0"
}

request.description:
Records an error the phone hit, under the phone's own `requestId` if it is a valid reference. Strict body: `message` (1-500 chars) required; optional `stack` (max 4000), `screen`, `requestId` (max 12), `appVersion` (max 20).

No login required, because the error can come from the login screen; the collection's Bearer token is still sent, so a signed-in report is attributed to the account. Own, stricter rate limit than the rest of the API.
The caller's own last 50 request log rows, newest first. Never anyone else's.

item.name: Trips
item.description: A trip groups expenses split with people (`type: person` accounts) and their settle-ups. `members` and every person id are person-account ids; create them under Accounts → Create person account (saves `{{personId}}`). Amounts are integer paise. Most writes are `400` on a **closed** trip until it is reopened.

request.description: Trips (active first, then newest) with totals and open balances, plus the all-trips summary with a figure per year.

Strict body. `name` (1-60), `startDate`, `endDate` (not before the start), `members` (up to 30 person-account ids; **every one must be a live person account**), optional `emoji`, `color`, `budget` (paise, min 0, or null). Test script saves `data._id` → `{{tripId}}`.
One trip in full: what it cost you, who owes whom, where your share went, the day-by-day figures and every expense and settle-up.
Any create field, all optional, strict. Removing a member who is already in an expense or settle-up is `400`.
Deletes the trip. `data` is null.

Strict body.
- `title` (1-80), `occurredAt`, `cost` (positive paise), optional `category` (an expense-category id or null).
- `paidBy`: a member id, or **null for you**.
- `paidFrom`: required when `paidBy` is null — one of your own accounts (bank, cash, wallet or credit card).
- `shares`: 1-31 rows of `{ account, amount }`; `account` is a member id or **null for your own share**; each person once; the amounts **must add up to `cost`** (`400` otherwise).

Your share becomes your spending; the rest becomes money owed. Test script saves `data._id` → `{{tripExpenseId}}`.
Replaces the expense: the body is the **same full shape** as Add trip expense (not a partial). The ledger rows it stood for are reverted and rewritten.
Reverts the expense's ledger rows and removes it.

Records a repayment. Strict body: `person` (a member id), `account` (one of your own accounts), `amount` (positive paise), `direction` (`received` = they paid you, `paid` = you paid them), optional `occurredAt`.

Sets what each person is expected to pay, per person and signed: positive = they pay you, negative = you pay them. Anyone left out pays nothing. The server validates the plan against the ledger (`400` with the reason if it does not fit). Response message: `Matched to Splitwise`.
Goes back to the exact amounts from the expenses. Response message: `Back to the exact amounts`.

Closes the trip; always allowed. Optional body `letGo`: person ids whose leftover balance is written off rather than kept (default none). Kept balances stay on each person's account to be settled later.

2.8.6: optional `closedOn` (`YYYY-MM-DD`): the day the trip counts on, as one expense in Trips. Default: its last expense day, kept between the trip's start day and today; outside that range is 400 `invalid_input`.

2.8.6. Moves a closed trip's one entry in Trips to another day without reopening it. Body `{ closedOn: "YYYY-MM-DD" }`, from the trip's start day to today in your zone (400 `invalid_input` outside). 409 when the trip isn't closed.
Reopens a closed trip for changes. No body.

Splitwise group export as CSV text. With **no `mapping`**, answers `{ needsMapping: true, people, suggested }`: the names found in the file and a best guess at who each is. `csv` is 1 byte to 2 MB.

Expected columns: `Date,Description,Category,Cost,Currency,<Person A>,<Person B>,…`. Rows each person's effect on their balance; `Payment` rows are settle-ups; the last row is `Total balance`.

Same CSV with a `mapping` from each name in the file to `"me"`, one of your person-account ids, or `"new"` (create them). Exactly one name must map to `me` (`400` otherwise). Answers the review rows, each with a `key`, a `status` and your share, plus `myShare`, `balance` and whether it `matchesFile`. A closed trip is `400`.

Commits the reviewed rows. Strict body: the same `csv` and `mapping`, plus `decisions` (up to 1000), one per row to act on:
- `key`: the row's `key` from the preview.
- `action`: `import` | `skip` | `apply` (apply a split to an expense you already logged).
- optional `category`, `title` (max 80), `account` (which of your accounts paid, for a row you paid), and `parts` (split one row into up to 20 parts, each `{ title, category, cost }`).

Re-importing the same file adds only rows not already in, by fingerprint.
